samples.summary: New `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` call on the image mousedown path has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds a new public `TextEditor.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` and calls it from `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2614) specifically so a read-only viewer clicking a *hyperlinked image* still follows the link on mouseup — the behavior the new `stopImmediatePropagation()`-in-read-only path would otherwise take away. Nothing exercises it: grep for `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse` matches only src/view/text-editor.ts, src/view/editor.ts and design docs; grep for `readOnlyPendingLinkHref|openLink|window.open` under packages/docs finds only src/view/text-editor.ts (no test). copy-integrity.test.ts never dispatches a mousedown that hits an image, and never involves a link inline. If this call regresses, viewers silently lose link-following on images with no failing test.
searchedFor: glob packages/docs/test/view/*.ts (link-run.test.ts, table-link.test.ts, editor-read-only.test.ts inspected via grep)

samples.summary: The headline new capability — a read-only click on an image body selects it — is never driven through mousedown; every test uses the `selectImageAt` API
samples.evidence: Removing `if (readOnly) return` from `handleImageMouseDown` is what lets a viewer select an image by clicking it. All 40+ image tests call `editor.selectImageAt('b1', 2)` (copy-integrity.test.ts:377…1091), which bypasses `findImageAtPoint`, the `e.preventDefault()/stopImmediatePropagation()` claim, `selectImageInline`'s focus, and `cursor.moveTo`. The one mousedown test (line 989) is deliberately a *miss* that takes the clear branch, so the hit branch (case 2 in the handler) has zero coverage in either mode.

samples.summary: The find-bar's new `editor?.clearImageSelection()` calls before replace/replaceAll are untested, and a docs test comment implies otherwise
samples.evidence: `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` gain `editor?.clearImageSelection()`. There is no test file for the find bar: glob packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/* lists no docs-find-bar test, and grep for `clearImageSelection` in tests matches only packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts. That test ('the exported clearImageSelection drops it, for out-of-module mutators', line 1084) only calls `editor.clearImageSelection()` directly while its comment claims to cover 'the seam they use instead (docs-find-bar.tsx)' — it cannot fail if the find bar drops the call, so the wiring is uncovered while reading as covered.

samples.summary: `applySpellSuggestion` and `insertPageNumber` gain image-selection clears with no test, while sibling mutators (paste/insertTable/insertImage/insertLink) all got one
samples.evidence: The 'mutations that shift the offsets under an image selection' describe block (copy-integrity.test.ts:1011-1099) covers paste, insertTable, insertImage, insertLink and the exported clearer, but not `applySpellSuggestion` (editor.ts ~3441) or `insertPageNumber` (editor.ts ~3831), both of which the diff also gates. Grep for `applySpellSuggestion` in tests finds only frontend toolbar/context-menu stubs; `insertPageNumber` appears in frontend toolbar tests only.

samples.summary: The null-`clipboardData` bail is only tested with an image selection; the text-selection case (where cut would have deleted content that reached no clipboard) is untested
samples.evidence: `handleCopy`/`handleCut` now read `e.clipboardData` before `preventDefault()`, affecting the text path too. The two tests using `{ withData: false }` (copy-integrity.test.ts:440 and 718) both set up an *image* selection via `selectImageAt` and no text selection, so they exit through the image branch. No test dispatches a null-clipboardData cut with a live text selection — exactly the case the comment says 'destroys content that reached no clipboard'.

samples.summary: DocCanvas's read-only wiring to `drawImageSelection(..., { handles: !this.readOnly })` is not covered; only the standalone overlay function is
samples.evidence: image-selection-overlay.test.ts adds a case calling `drawImageSelection(ctx, rect, { handles: false })` directly, but nothing asserts DocCanvas actually forwards its `readOnly` flag (doc-canvas.ts:683) or that `editor.ts` passes `readOnly` into `new DocCanvas`. The copy-integrity tests use a no-op Proxy 2d context, so no drawing is observable there. A wiring regression (e.g. passing `handles: this.readOnly`) would show handles to viewers with a green suite.
searchedFor: read diff hunks for doc-canvas.ts and image-selection-overlay.test.ts

samples.summary: New read-only guards in `handleImageResizeMouseMove`/`MouseUp` and `handleImageHover` have no tests
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (readOnly || !imageResizeDrag) return` (editor.ts ~2471), a `if (readOnly) { render(); return; }` bail before the resize commit (~2512), and `if (readOnly) return false` in `handleImageHover` (~2764). copy-integrity.test.ts never dispatches mousemove/mouseup/resize-drag or hover events (no `mousemove`/`mouseup` dispatch anywhere in the file), and no other docs test references `imageResizeDrag`. These are defense-in-depth guards, so failure is contained, but nothing would notice if one were removed.

samples.summary: The added `render()` in the key catch-all is not asserted; the F5 test only checks the selection flag
samples.evidence: editor.ts's catch-all now calls `render()` after clearing `selectedImage`, justified by 'a key TextEditor ignores would otherwise leave the selection overlay painted'. The covering test ('a non-modifier key still drops the image selection', line 975) asserts only `getSelectedImage()` is null — it would pass with the `render()` removed, i.e. with the stale-overlay bug present.

samples.summary: 'insertTable clears it' asserts only the clear, not that the insert happened, so it cannot detect the clear running on a no-op path
samples.evidence: The test calls `editor.insertTable(2, 2)` and asserts only `getSelectedImage()` toBeNull. `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` is the first statement in `insertTable`, so the assertion holds even if the table insertion silently no-ops (e.g. cursor unset). Adding an assertion that a table block now exists would tie the clear to the mutation it is supposed to precede. Same shape as the neighbouring insertImage/insertLink tests, which also assert only the clear.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: editor.ts:2614 calls the new public TextEditor.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse (text-editor.ts:1637-1640) from the image-body-hit branch of handleImageMouseDown, immediately before stopImmediatePropagation, specifically so a read-only viewer clicking a hyperlinked image still follows the link on mouseup. No test exercises it. Repo-wide grep for recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse matches only the two source files plus design/task markdown; grep for readOnlyPendingLinkHref|getLinkHrefAtMouse|window.open matches no test file anywhere in the repo. Only two docs tests mention readOnly: editor-read-only.test.ts (read in full — dispatches only input/clipboard/keyboard events, and its own header says pointer/link paths are left to manual/browser tests) and copy-integrity.test.ts, whose single mousedown dispatch (line 1000) is at clientX/clientY 0,0 and is documented as deliberately missing every image, so it takes the clear-and-fall-through branch and never enters the image-hit branch holding the new call; its read-only image-copy test (line 429) uses the programmatic selectImageAt API and bypasses handleImageMouseDown entirely. 'mouseup' is never dispatched anywhere under packages/docs/test, so the follow-through half is untested too. No e2e suites and no co-located src test files exist. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a new user-facing interaction path (viewer link-following on hyperlinked images) can regress silently with no failing test, and it is testable in jsdom since the same suite already constructs image blocks and dispatches container mousedowns.
